faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about PréviSéisme Caraïbe.

items.question: Where does the displayed seismic data come from?
items.answer: We continuously aggregate public feeds from USGS (United States), EMSC (Europe/Mediterranean), IPGP (Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris, Antilles network) and the international FDSN network.

items.question: Can PréviSéisme Caraïbe predict an earthquake?
items.answer: No. No current technology can reliably predict the date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake. Our platform focuses on fast detection, reliable aggregation and risk analysis based on seismic history.

items.question: Is the service free?
items.answer: Public access (map, search, history, personal alerts) is free. Paid plans exist for businesses and local authorities with advanced multi-site monitoring needs.

items.question: How are confidence levels calculated?
items.answer: Each event is compared across the available sources. The more an event is confirmed by several independent networks with consistent parameters, the higher its confidence level.

items.question: Can I use the data via an API?
items.answer: Yes, a public REST API is available. See the API page for full documentation and to obtain an access key.

items.question: In which languages is the platform available?
items.answer: PréviSéisme Caraïbe is available in French, English and Spanish, with French as the default language.

items.question: How do I report that I felt an earthquake?
items.answer: On each event's detail page, an "I felt this earthquake" button lets you contribute to estimating the intensity perceived on the ground.

items.question: Is my personal data protected?
items.answer: Yes. We apply strict data protection principles and never share your personal information with third parties without explicit consent.
